summary:
La Libertad stands under Peru's national framework, which governs identity documents, facility access and discrimination law; this assessment covers only what is specific to the region. Two documents carry the region-specific record: a national prosecution study that disaggregates homicides of LGTB people by prosecution district, and a 2024 regional ordinance on labour inclusion. Neither establishes a regional anti-discrimination enforcement mechanism, and no region-specific data on policing, restroom-law enforcement or service access appears in the sources.

The Public Prosecutor's Office published a study of intentional deaths of LGTB people between 2012 and 2021, drawn from 84 criminal complaints covering 88 victims and 72 identified suspects. Six fiscal districts accounted for 58% of the deaths. La Libertad recorded 10, second only to Lima's 12 and level with Lima Norte, ahead of Lima Este (7), Lima Sur (6) and Callao (6). The ranking is by raw count. La Libertad is one of Peru's more populous regions, and the study supplies no per-capita denominator, so the figure does not by itself show that a trans visitor faces higher risk in La Libertad than in a smaller district. The study was produced with the Justice Ministry's human-rights office and the Cayetano Heredia University LGTB-rights observatory with UNDP support.

Ordenanza Regional N.° 009-2024-GRLL-CR, approved in Trujillo on 6 September 2024 and published in El Peruano on 7 November 2024, promotes the labour inclusion of travesti, transsexual and transgender people in La Libertad. It declares their right to formal, dignified and productive work in equitable and satisfactory conditions without discrimination on grounds of gender identity or its expression, and recognises the trans community as a group in a situation of vulnerability in the region. It is a positive-action measure addressed to employment, not a protection a visitor can invoke against police, service providers or private venues, and it specifies no penalty or enforcement body.

The ordinance recommends that local governments issue municipal ordinances recognising gender identity and fundamental rights, and orders a working group (mesa de trabajo) to be convened. It cites constitutional equality guarantees and article 323 of the Penal Code on discrimination, and recalls a 2014 regional-council session that set a framework against discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity. Whether any La Libertad municipality has acted on the recommendation is not documented in the sources.
tangentialFactors:
The regional ordinance's legal basis is article 323 of the Penal Code, the discrimination provision it cites. Whether that article currently provides an enforceable route is a question of national law rather than regional practice, and the ordinance itself creates no regional offence or complaint route.

La Libertad's regional government has recognised trans people as a vulnerable group and adopted a labour-inclusion policy, while district-level prosecution data place the region among those with the highest raw counts of recorded LGTB homicides. The recognition is a policy statement by the regional government; the homicide figures come from the national prosecution service. No source connects the two or documents a regional response to the recorded deaths.
localsOnly:
Ordenanza Regional N.° 009-2024-GRLL-CR was presented in the regional council's ordinary session of 3 September 2024, debated, approved and signed in Trujillo on 6 September 2024, and entered into force the day after its publication in El Peruano on 7 November 2024. Its object is positive-action measures for the effective labour inclusion of travesti, transsexual and transgender persons in La Libertad.

The ordinance grounds the right in constitutional equality guarantees and article 323 of the Penal Code, and recalls a 2014 regional-council session that established a framework against discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity. It recommends that local governments issue municipal ordinances recognising gender identity and fundamental rights, and orders a working group (mesa de trabajo). It states no penalty, no oversight body and no reporting requirement.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source documents enforcement of the 2024 ordinance, the composition or output of its working group, or any municipal ordinance adopted in La Libertad under its recommendation.

No region-specific data on restroom or facility access, police conduct or health-service access in La Libertad appears in the inventory.

The prosecution study's recommendations, including training for criminal prosecutors on identifying LGTB victims and monitoring systems, are national measures; no La Libertad-specific implementation is documented.

The ordinance cites article 323 of the Penal Code as its discrimination basis; whether that article currently provides an enforceable route is a question of national law and is not resolved by the regional sources.
